title: Resend POST abuse posture (AD-15 fake-success) has no handler-level test; answer POST path is asymmetrically pinned
evidence:
handle_resend branch:
    application_handler.is_honeypot_filled(values)
    || is_resend_timing_suspicious(values)
  {
    // Fake success: a bot sees the same page a referee sees after a send.
    True -> form_pages.view_resent() |> ssr_response.to_sensitive_response

Asymmetry — the answer POST bot path IS pinned (server/test/integration/reference_form_integration_test.gleam:459 `honeypot_filled_post_saves_nothing_test`, :484 `missing_timing_post_saves_nothing_test`, body fills `#("_website", "http://spam.example")`), but every resend test calls `handle_resend` with clean `timing_fields()` (`#("_website", "")`); grep for resend+honeypot/timing/bot returns only the pure-predicate unit test (form_handler_test.gleam:304-314 `is_resend_timing_suspicious`), never the handler's silent-drop-with-fake-success branch.
detail: AC6 pins the abuse posture on both answer AND resend POSTs. The predicate is unit-tested, but the handler's fake-`view_resent`-without-remint behaviour is unpinned; a regression dropping the honeypot guard would let bots trigger token remints.
recommended_fix: Add an integration test mirroring honeypot_filled_post_saves_nothing_test for POST /reference/:token/resend: fill _website, assert 200 + data-testid=reference-resent AND no remint (form_token unchanged) + no audit row.
